Hi Marta —

Thanks for sending the redlines. Attached is an initial draft of the Redwood security exhibit that maps our standard artifacts to common customer checklists (redwood_security_exhibit_draft_v1.docx). High level proposals:

- SOC 2: we provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report on request and offer an annual update; for customers needing more continuous proofs we can provide scoped log extracts and control evidence on a regular cadence (weekly or monthly) under an NDA and limited access arrangement.
- Pen test / inspection: we support a staged approach — a 2–4 week notice period for infrastructure-level tests, 1–2 week notice for application-level tests. We prefer tests run against a dedicated staging slice with transient credentials and explicit scope.
- Evidence cadence & artifacts: propose a 4–6 week evidence sprint for initial onboarding (architecture diagrams, control mappings, SOC report, support runbooks). After that, recurring evidence bundles (monthly or quarterly) as agreed in the Order Form.

Proposed next steps:
1) Legal redline pass on the attached exhibit (Laura, can you review the liability/inspection language?)
2) Ops to confirm pen-test ops and staging readiness (Soojin, can you outline the minimum handoff doc?)
3) Schedule a 30‑minute kickoff to agree owners and timelines.

If that sounds reasonable I can turn this into tracked redlines for the MSA + Order Form.

— Markus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Markus / Marta — quick legal read. I reviewed the draft and Arbor's redlines. Key asks and suggested language:

1) Inspection scope: replace broad "audit rights" with a scoped inspection clause limited to (a) SOC 2 artifacts, (b) configuration snapshots for customer‑facing services, and (c) logs relevant to customer accounts. Add explicit sampling language: "Customer may request evidence for up to X sample sets per year; Redwood will provide artifacts subject to redaction for other customers' data."

2) Pen test windows: accept a 30–60 day notice window for infrastructure tests, but require the customer to use only preapproved testing vendors and to sign the Redwood pen-test ops addendum. We will refuse tests that target production with live customer traffic unless a dedicated maintenance window is scheduled.

3) Confidentiality & retention: evidence delivered for audits will be covered by standard confidentiality and retention terms; ask to include a carveout for ephemeral evidence (e.g., raw logs exposed for an audit will be purged after 90 days).

I've inline‑commented the attached draft (I'll share via Drive) and recommend we offer a 2‑tier evidence cadence in the Order Form: onboarding sprint (6 weeks) + recurring quarterly bundles.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Marta / Team — ops perspective on what we can reliably commit to and the handoff we'd need from Arbor: 

- Pen-test ops: We require a 14–30 day test window (shorter windows for app-level), a staging environment that mirrors production performance for latencies, and an agreed fail/stop criteria matrix. We will provide a test account, S3 bucket (if needed), and a temporary service account with limited privileges.
- Evidence deliverables (initial onboarding sprint): 1) SOC 2 Type II report, 2) control mapping to Redwood product features, 3) infra diagrams, 4) sample audit logs (7 days of scrubbed logs), 5) runbooks for incident response.
- Ongoing cadence: monthly tokenized logs for a rolling 90‑day window + quarterly control snapshots.

Operational asks of Arbor: list of approved testers and expected test types, a signed pen-test addendum, and a primary technical contact for scheduling.

I can assemble the handoff checklist and a lightweight runbook by EOW.
